tasks.short: Match purchase orders and goods receipts to supplier invoices in AFAS, then book and route them for approval.

today.trigger: Supplier invoice arrives as PDF in the AP mailbox or on a staffing agency portal.
steps: Open the PDF from the shared Outlook AP mailbox
Look up the order in AFAS and check quantities, prices and VAT
Compare agency invoices with approved flex hours from the portal
Enter header and lines in AFAS and route to the budget holder
Email the supplier or site manager when something does not match
drudgery: Chasing site managers for goods receipt confirmation
Checking flex hours line by line against agency invoices
today.time_sinks: Agency invoices with hundreds of hour lines and invoices without an order number.

lenses.faster: OCR plus an LLM reads the invoice and a matching rule does the three-way match; the bookkeeper only opens invoices that fail tolerance.
lenses.autonomous: Every new invoice in the AP mailbox is read, matched and booked as a draft entry in AFAS without anyone starting it.
lenses.ambitious: Check every agency hour line against the approved shift roster and the CAO rates, not a sample, and recover overbilling.
lenses.joy: No retyping; what is left is solving real mismatches with suppliers and sites.
lenses.options: For an unmatched invoice the tool proposes the three most likely orders or cost centres with reasons.
lenses.altitude: The bookkeeper sets the tolerances, supplier rules and exception queues and reviews the match rate weekly.
reach: Credit and Collections Officer: supplier statement disputes

tasks.human_edge: Judging whether a price difference is agreed, knowing which site manager to ask, and keeping supplier relationships good.
tasks.pattern_why: Reading PDFs needs a model, matching is rules, and exceptions need tools and follow-up; a person approves anything outside tolerance.

in_practice.trigger: New invoice in the AP mailbox or a new invoice file on an agency portal.
steps: Extract supplier, order number, lines, VAT and IBAN from the PDF
Match against AFAS orders and receipts, and agency invoices against approved hours
Book matched invoices within tolerance as draft entries for approval
Put mismatches in a queue with the difference explained
Draft the question to the supplier or site manager for the bookkeeper to send
in_practice.human_gate: Bookkeeper releases invoices outside tolerance, new suppliers and any changed IBAN; budget holder approval in AFAS stays.
in_practice.logs_to: AFAS audit trail plus a match log per invoice in SharePoint

evidence.claim: Invoice capture with automatic two- and three-way PO matching is sold as standard AP automation.
LLMs extract invoice fields reliably from varied PDF layouts.

risks: Fake or changed IBAN on an invoice passed automatically (payment fraud)
Agency hour data on portals not in a usable export format
Budget holders approving blindly because the tool already matched
research_questions: What share of last quarter's invoices carried a valid order number?
Can the three agency portals export approved hours as CSV or API?
Which capture tools have a tested AFAS Profit connector?

tasks.short: Post debits and credits in AFAS and keep running totals and checks in Excel.

today.trigger: Daily batches of invoices, bank lines and memorial entries to book.
steps: Collect source documents for the day
Post entries in AFAS memorial or purchase journals
Total batches in Excel and check against AFAS
Correct errors found in totals
drudgery: Hunting a small difference in a batch
today.time_sinks: Finding why an Excel total and the AFAS total differ by a few euros.

lenses.faster: Entries are generated by rules from source data and control totals are computed by AFAS reports instead of Excel.
lenses.autonomous: Recurring entries (rent, leases, depreciation, accruals) post on schedule and a check flags any batch that does not balance.
lenses.ambitious: Daily soft close: the ledger is correct every day, not only at month end.
lenses.joy: No more adding up columns twice; time goes to the entries that need thought.
lenses.options: For an unusual entry the tool shows two or three account and cost centre options with past examples.
lenses.altitude: The bookkeeper owns the posting rules and recurring entry templates and checks the exceptions report.

tasks.human_edge: Choosing the right account for unusual items and spotting entries that look correct but make no business sense.
tasks.pattern_why: Debit and credit logic and totals are fixed rules on structured data; no model is needed to run it.

in_practice.trigger: Scheduled daily run and month-end calendar.
steps: Generate recurring and rule-based entries in AFAS via import or connector
Run balance and control-total checks automatically
Flag unbalanced or unusual entries to the bookkeeper
Bookkeeper corrects and releases the batch
in_practice.human_gate: Bookkeeper releases flagged batches; Controller signs off the posting rules.
data_needed: Chart of accounts and cost centres
in_practice.logs_to: AFAS journal audit trail and a run log in SharePoint

evidence.claim: AFAS Profit supports periodic entries and data import through connectors.
evidence.source: AFAS Profit (model knowledge of product features)

risks: A wrong rule repeats an error every day until noticed
Less hands-on knowledge of the ledger among junior staff
research_questions: How many entries per month are recurring or rule-based today?
How much time goes into Excel control totals per week?
Does AFAS internal control reporting replace the Excel checks?

tasks.short: Code invoices and costs to the right ledger account, cost centre and site, and keep the records complete.

today.trigger: Each invoice, expense and bank line that needs coding.
steps: Read the document and decide account, cost centre and site
Enter coding in AFAS
Ask colleagues when the cost type is unclear
Summarise totals per site in Excel for the Controller
drudgery: Coding the same suppliers the same way every month
today.time_sinks: Unclear invoices (mixed sites, mixed cost types) and rework after Controller review.

lenses.faster: A model proposes coding from invoice text and coding history; the bookkeeper confirms only low-confidence ones.
lenses.autonomous: Coding for known suppliers with stable history is applied automatically and summaries come from Power BI.
lenses.ambitious: Consistent cost coding across Rotterdam, Tilburg and Venlo so cost per pallet per site can be compared properly for the first time.
lenses.joy: Repetitive coding goes; left is fixing the chart of accounts and helping managers read their costs.
lenses.options: Show top three coding suggestions with confidence and the past invoices they are based on.
lenses.altitude: The bookkeeper maintains the coding rules and reviews a monthly sample of auto-coded lines.
reach: FP&A Analyst: actuals per site for the forecast

tasks.human_edge: Knowing what a cost really is for and how a site manager will read it.
tasks.pattern_why: Free-text invoice lines to a structured account and cost centre, inside a deterministic booking flow with confidence thresholds.

in_practice.trigger: Invoice or bank line arrives without coding.
steps: Model reads description, supplier and history
Proposes account, cost centre, site and VAT code with confidence
High-confidence known patterns are applied, the rest queued
Bookkeeper confirms or corrects; corrections feed the history
in_practice.human_gate: Bookkeeper confirms low-confidence and new-supplier coding; monthly sample checked by the Controller.
data_needed: Chart of accounts and cost centre list
in_practice.logs_to: AFAS entry with suggestion and confidence stored in a coding log

evidence.claim: Bookkeeping tools learn coding from history and pre-fill ledger accounts.
LLMs classify invoice lines to a chart of accounts with good accuracy given examples.

risks: Silent miscoding that shifts costs between sites
VAT code errors leading to wrong BTW returns
research_questions: What share of invoices come from suppliers with stable coding history?
How many coding corrections did the Controller make last quarter?
Is the cost centre structure the same across the three sites?

tasks.short: Move totals from sub-ledgers, agency files and Excel sheets into the general ledger in AFAS.

today.trigger: Weekly and month-end transfers from sub-administrations and external files.
steps: Export data from agency portals and Excel sheets
Reformat into an AFAS import layout or type it in
Post the summary entries in the general ledger
Check the totals match the source
today.time_sinks: Source files that change layout without warning.

lenses.faster: Fixed scripts convert each source into the AFAS import format and post it; the step becomes a click.
lenses.autonomous: Files dropped in a SharePoint folder are converted, validated and posted as a draft journal.
lenses.ambitious: Remove the Excel layer altogether so every GL figure traces back to its source line.
lenses.joy: Nobody misses copy-paste; left is checking that the totals make sense.
lenses.options: When a layout changes, an LLM proposes the column mapping for the bookkeeper to confirm.
lenses.altitude: The bookkeeper owns the interface list and mappings and fixes them when sources change.
reach: People Analytics and HRIS Analyst: data pipelines into Power BI

tasks.human_edge: Recognising when a source total is wrong before it reaches the ledger.
tasks.pattern_why: Structured input, fixed mapping, checkable totals; build with AI coding help and run without a model.

in_practice.trigger: File arrives in a SharePoint drop folder or on a schedule.
steps: Validate file layout and totals
Map to AFAS import format
Post as draft journal in AFAS
Send a reconciliation summary to the bookkeeper
in_practice.human_gate: Bookkeeper releases the draft journal; mapping changes need Controller approval.
systems: Power Automate or a small script
in_practice.logs_to: Import log in SharePoint and AFAS audit trail

evidence.claim: AFAS Profit accepts journal entries via import and connectors (UpdateConnectors).

risks: Silent failure when a source layout changes
Script owned by one person with no documentation
research_questions: How many distinct sources feed the GL by hand today?
Who will maintain the scripts when the bookkeeper is away?
How often did source layouts change in the past year?

tasks.short: Reconcile bank, supplier and customer accounts and report differences to the Controller.

today.trigger: Daily Rabobank statements, monthly supplier statements and month-end close.
steps: Import Rabobank statements into AFAS
Match bank lines to open items by hand where automatic matching fails
Compare supplier statements with AFAS open items
List differences in Excel and email the Controller or supplier
drudgery: Matching customer payments with wrong or missing references
Ticking off supplier statements line by line
today.time_sinks: Partial payments and payments covering several invoices.

lenses.faster: Rules match most bank lines; an LLM reads payment remarks and remittance emails for the rest.
lenses.autonomous: Each morning the bank file is matched and a difference list is ready before the bookkeeper starts.
lenses.ambitious: Reconcile every supplier statement every month instead of only the big suppliers.
lenses.joy: No more ticking off lists; left is the investigation of real differences.
lenses.options: For an unmatched payment, propose the likely invoice combinations that add up to the amount.
lenses.altitude: The bookkeeper tunes the matching rules and owns the reconciliation status in Power BI.
reach: Credit and Collections Officer: cash application and dispute follow-up

tasks.human_edge: Deciding what a difference means and whether to write off, chase or escalate it.
tasks.pattern_why: Matching is rules, but unclear references, remittance emails and follow-up need reading and tools; write-offs need a person.

in_practice.trigger: New Rabobank statement (CAMT.053) or supplier statement received.
steps: Auto-match bank lines on amount, reference and IBAN
LLM reads remarks and remittance mails for unmatched lines
Propose matches and invoice combinations
Queue differences with explanation and draft supplier query
in_practice.human_gate: Bookkeeper confirms proposed matches; write-offs above a threshold go to the Controller.
in_practice.logs_to: AFAS matching history and difference log in SharePoint

evidence.claim: AFAS Profit imports bank statements and matches payments to open items automatically.
Cash application tools use AI to match payments to invoices.

risks: Wrong match hides an unpaid invoice
Over-reliance makes small recurring differences invisible
research_questions: What share of bank lines match automatically in AFAS today?
How many supplier statements are reconciled per month now?
Are remittance advices mostly email, PDF or portal?

tasks.short: Book the AFAS payroll journal, pay net wages and taxes, and check agency flex costs.

today.trigger: Monthly and four-weekly payroll runs by the Payroll Specialist.
steps: Receive the payroll journal from AFAS payroll
Check it against headcount and last period
Prepare the net wage and loonheffing payment batch in Rabobank
Reconcile payroll liabilities (tax, pension, CAO funds)
drudgery: Rebuilding the same variance checks every run
Reconciling pension and fund payables by hand
today.time_sinks: Explaining differences between periods with shift allowances and flex peaks.

lenses.faster: Variance checks per cost centre and liability reconciliations run automatically after each payroll run.
lenses.autonomous: After the payroll run closes, the journal is posted as draft and the variance report goes to the bookkeeper and Payroll Specialist.
lenses.ambitious: Total labour cost per site per week, own staff plus flex, available to managers for the first time.
lenses.joy: No repeat spreadsheet checks; left is explaining real changes.
lenses.options: Show the variance split by cause: headcount, overtime, shift allowance, flex.
lenses.altitude: The bookkeeper designs the payroll control set and reviews it with the Payroll Specialist.

tasks.human_edge: Payment release responsibility, confidentiality of pay data and judgement on unusual variances.
tasks.pattern_why: Payroll journals and liabilities are structured; checks are fixed rules. Pay data stays out of general LLM tools.

steps: Post payroll journal as draft
Run variance and liability checks
Build payment batch for review
Send exceptions to bookkeeper and Payroll Specialist
in_practice.human_gate: Four-eyes release of the Rabobank payment batch; Payroll Specialist confirms variances.
in_practice.logs_to: AFAS audit trail and payroll control checklist in SharePoint

evidence.claim: AFAS Profit integrates payroll with the general ledger and produces the payroll journal.

risks: AVG/GDPR: pay data exposed beyond need-to-know
Payment errors on net wages hit employees directly
research_questions: Which payroll checks are done today and how long do they take?
Is the payroll-to-GL posting already automatic in AFAS?
Who holds the Rabobank release rights and is four-eyes enforced?

tasks.short: Create customer invoices for warehousing and transport, and send statements and reminders.

today.trigger: Month end and shipment completion; customer contract terms.
steps: Collect storage, handling and transport volumes from operations
Apply contract rates and surcharges in Excel
Create invoices in AFAS and email them
Send account statements and first reminders
drudgery: Re-sending invoices to the right customer address
today.time_sinks: Collecting volume data from three sites and checking surcharges like fuel.

lenses.faster: Rate cards in a table and volume exports from the WMS produce invoice lines automatically.
lenses.autonomous: At month end invoices are generated as drafts; statements and first reminders go out on schedule.
lenses.ambitious: Bill every billable activity (extra handling, waiting time) that now slips through, lowering DSO and revenue leakage.
lenses.joy: No manual rate maths; left is customer contact on disputes.
lenses.options: An LLM drafts reminder texts in different tones per customer history.
lenses.altitude: The bookkeeper maintains rate cards and billing rules and reviews draft runs.
reach: Credit and Collections Officer: first-line dunning

tasks.human_edge: Knowing customer agreements not yet in the system and handling disputes with tact.
tasks.pattern_why: Volumes times contracted rates is rule-based; only reminder wording benefits from a model.

in_practice.trigger: Month end or shipment closed in operations.
steps: Pull volumes per customer from operational exports
Apply rate card and surcharges
Create draft invoices in AFAS
Bookkeeper reviews outliers, then send
Statements and reminders follow a schedule
in_practice.human_gate: Bookkeeper approves invoices with outliers versus last month; credit notes approved by the Controller.
in_practice.logs_to: AFAS sales journal and billing run log

evidence.claim: AFAS Profit supports subscription and project-based invoicing with automated reminders.

risks: Wrong rate card billed to many customers at once
Customer complaints if reminders go out on disputed invoices
research_questions: What share of billable activities is captured today?
Are contract rates stored anywhere structured?
Can operations deliver volume data per customer automatically?

tasks.short: Enter purchase orders for sites and check and book staff expense claims.

today.trigger: Requests from site managers by email and expense claims submitted by staff.
steps: Receive purchase requests by email or Teams
Create the PO in AFAS with supplier and budget
Check expense receipts against policy
Book and pay approved expenses
drudgery: Checking receipts against the expense policy

lenses.faster: An LLM turns an email request into a draft PO and reads receipts against the expense policy.
lenses.autonomous: Requests via a form create draft POs; expenses within policy are booked after manager approval.
lenses.ambitious: All spend through POs, so commitments are visible to FP&A before invoices arrive.
lenses.joy: No more chasing missing details; left is advising sites on suppliers.
lenses.options: Propose preferred suppliers and earlier prices for each request.
lenses.altitude: The bookkeeper owns the request form, policy rules and the exceptions queue.
reach: FP&A Analyst: committed spend in forecast

tasks.human_edge: Judging policy edge cases and saying no to colleagues tactfully.
tasks.pattern_why: Unstructured requests and receipts become structured POs and checks inside a fixed approval flow.

in_practice.trigger: Purchase request form or expense claim submitted.
steps: Extract items, supplier, amount and cost centre
Check budget and expense policy
Create draft PO or expense entry in AFAS
Send to approver; flag policy exceptions
in_practice.human_gate: Budget holder approves POs; bookkeeper decides policy exceptions.

evidence.claim: Expense tools read receipts and check them against policy.

risks: Policy checks too strict or too lax without tuning
research_questions: How many POs and expense claims per month, and how many incomplete?
Does AFAS workflow already cover expense approval?
Will site managers use a request form?

role.altitude: From entering and matching transactions to running the AP/AR automation: owning matching rules, coding rules, interfaces and exception queues, and reporting match rates and differences to the Controller.
reach: Credit and Collections Officer: cash application and first-line dunning
Accountant: recurring entries, accruals and balance sheet reconciliations
FP&A Analyst: actuals and committed spend feeds
role.ceiling_note: Out of roughly 1,600 hours per FTE these eight tasks are about 400; perhaps 220 to 250 of those can go. The ceiling is exceptions, supplier and customer relationships, fraud and payment release responsibility, and the quality of AFAS master data and agency data.
skills_to_grow: Designing and testing rules and tolerances
AFAS connectors and Power Automate basics
role.ambitious_version: A daily soft close: every invoice, bank line and agency hour checked on the day it arrives, full flex-cost audit against rosters and CAO rates, and a ledger the Controller can trust any day, cutting close time and DSO.
